ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and points $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ are on the same line, with $CG=CD$, $DF=DE$. What is the measure of $\angle EFD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB=60^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle ACB=\angle CGD+\angle CDG$,\\
it follows that $\angle CGD+\angle CDG=60^\circ$.\\
Since $CG=CD$,\\
it follows that $\angle CGD=\angle CDG=30^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle CDG=\angle DFE+\angle E$,\\
it follows that $\angle DFE+\angle E=30^\circ$.\\
Since $DF=DE$,\\
it follows that $\angle DFE=\angle E=15^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle EFD=\boxed{15^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, B, C, D, E are located on the same horizontal straight line; A is above, and AB, AC and BC form triangle ABC. Point G is marked on side AC; there is an oblique line from G to D, and point F is located on this oblique line segment; additionally, a line segment is drawn from F to E, so what is required is the angle ∠EFD at point F in triangle DFE. Reasoning: Because △ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠ACB = 60°. At point C, CG is along the direction of CA, and CD is the reverse extension line of CB, so ∠GCD = 180° - 60° = 120°. In △CGD, it is known that CG = CD, therefore △CGD is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, namely ∠CGD = ∠CDG. Thus ∠CGD + ∠CDG = 180° - 120° = 60°, so ∠CDG = 30°. Also because F is on DG, and E is on the extension line of DC, ∠CDG is the exterior angle at point D of △DFE, therefore ∠CDG = ∠DFE + ∠DEF. Hence ∠DFE + ∠DEF = 30°. It is known that DF = DE, so △DFE is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠DFE and ∠DEF are equal. Therefore 2∠EFD = 30°, obtaining ∠EFD = 15°.
